subtopic: Deciding whether to report a cheating friend
subtype: Approach: reporting through the proper channel calmly [Action]
passage:
Counsellor's note. Maria came in at 1:15 with a sheet of paper. She said she had spoken to her friend twice about copying in tests, and the friend had refused to stop. She gave me the dates and what she saw, without adding opinions or naming anyone else. When I asked why now, she said, “I'm worried, not angry. I don't want anyone punished for fun. I just want it fair.” I thanked her, and explained that I would pass it to the class teacher, that the matter would be handled fairly with the friend heard too, and that she does not need to join any meeting. I offered to see her again in a week, because friendships strain. She asked whether the friend would know it was her. I said the school handles that carefully but I could not promise.
— Usha, school counsellor

qa.q: How many times had Maria spoken to her friend about copying?
qa.a: Maria had spoken to her friend twice about copying in tests.

qa.q: What does Maria's wording, worried not angry, suggest about what she feels?
qa.a: Maria feels concerned rather than vengeful: she says she is worried, not angry, gave dates and facts without opinions, and only wants things to be fair.

qa.q: What could the school do to support Maria and the friend?
qa.a: The school could handle the matter fairly and hear the friend too, and offer both a check-in with the counsellor.

qa.q: How might the friend feel when the class teacher raises the copying?
qa.a: The friend may feel embarrassed, angry or scared, but a fair hearing where the friend can explain may make it easier to change.

grounding: After the friend refuses to stop, a teen tells the counsellor factually, without gossip, saying she is worried rather than vengeful.

passage:
Thursday
Did it today. I told Mrs Bhutia.
Two weeks ago I talked to Vikas privately about the phone in his pocket during tests. He laughed and said everyone does it and I should mind my own business. Last Monday I saw it again, in the geography test.
So after school I went to the staffroom. I'd practised it: only facts. “In the last two tests, I saw Vikas reading from his phone under the desk. I talked to him first, two weeks ago, and he didn't stop.” I didn't repeat any of the things the other kids say about him. I told her I wasn't trying to get him into trouble; I was worried he'd get caught in the boards, where it's much worse, and that it isn't fair to the others.
She thanked me and said she'd handle it fairly and wouldn't say who told.
I feel sick and relieved at the same time.
– Dolma

qa.q: What did Vikas say when Dolma talked to him privately?
qa.a: He laughed and said everyone does it.

qa.q: How did Dolma feel after telling Mrs Bhutia?
qa.a: Dolma felt sick and relieved at the same time.

qa.q: What made the way Dolma reported it fair?
qa.a: Sticking to facts, mentioning the earlier private talk, and explaining the worry instead of repeating gossip.

qa.q: How might Mrs Bhutia see Dolma's report?
qa.a: Mrs Bhutia sees a calm, factual report from a worried student, which makes it easier to handle fairly.

grounding: Shows a teen who, after the friend refuses to stop, reports it to the teacher factually and without gossip, making clear the worry is not revenge.

Swati: i'm going to the counsellor tomorrow about Rhea
Pooja: the copying thing?
Swati: yes. i talked to her last week like we said. she told me to back off and did it again in the maths test
Pooja: are you sure? she'll know it's you
Swati: maybe. but i'm not posting about it or telling the whole class. just the counsellor
Pooja: what will you say
Swati: only what i saw. two tests, notes in her pencil box. and that i talked to her first
Swati: and that i'm worried about her, not trying to get revenge
Pooja: ok. that's fair actually
(next day)
Swati: done. i asked for it to be handled fairly, without everyone knowing
Swati: counsellor said she'll speak to Rhea privately and won't name me
Pooja: proud of you

qa.q: Where were Rhea's notes during the tests?
What might Swati be feeling the night before?
qa.a: Swati is probably nervous that Rhea will know, but determined to be fair and worried for Rhea.

qa.q: Why is going to the counsellor better than posting about it?
qa.a: It keeps it private and fair, letting an adult handle it without humiliating Rhea in front of the class.

qa.q: How does Pooja's view change during the chat?
qa.a: Pooja starts doubtful and worried for Swati, then calls the plan fair and ends up proud.
